rows.grounds: object of seeking; accusative singular of dharma
first person plural present middle indicative of √ī (to go, seek, implore)

items.question: What righteous principle do the supplicants implore in this petition?
premises: The verb īmahe expresses a collective act of seeking or imploring.
The object dharmam denotes righteous order or sacred duty.
The petition follows a request for a remedy in the preceding context.
items.inference: The supplicants collectively implore the attainment or bestowal of righteous order.
uncertainties: Whether dharmam refers to moral duty, cosmic order, or ritual law in this specific context is not fully determined.
